summary: Proof-worth registry entries owned by the sovereign operation control plane.

entries.contract: Closed operation schemas retain generation-bound operation, resource, stream, tap-target, producer-backed artifact custody, recovery, and same-UID barrier state. Tap remains specifically unavailable; fixed video recording admits producer-backed reveal, remove, and release while retain remains specifically unavailable. The request envelope admits asserted_attribution only on its closed creation surfaces; malformed, unknown, mechanical-authority, and human-intent fields are rejected.
entries.worth: This catches wire drift, source-free tap success, custody success without an admitted producer, missing generation or target-state fields, policy leakage, raw-content event leakage, and widening of private external-spawn actions before a runtime client can depend on them.

That grammar validates the closed generic attribution flags before spawn and carries them only on the exact operation-creation envelope. The parent-only token admits a child only after dynamic Node.js Foundation SecCode and mapped-vnode verification; only then does the dispatcher write the reviewed in-memory module bundle, and tokenless finalization resolves the exact admitted socket-peer generation. Parent abandon, bounded expiry, and boot recovery terminalize unfinalized prepared operation/resource claims. External dispatch propagates only the reviewed OPERATION_BARRIER_CLOSED and OPERATION_RESOURCE_BUSY intent failures; arbitrary daemon error strings remain collapsed.
entries.worth: This prevents PID reuse, basename/path trust, caller-selected or substituted Node interpreters, raw executable/script/helper identity persistence, substituted reviewed dependencies, token delivery to the child, finalize-before-image-admission, stale prepared microphone claims, untyped barrier/resource conflicts, and a transient external adapter from escaping its mechanically authenticated owner root.
